Reset contained entity alerts?

Contained entity alerts will be enabled, all existing alert rules will be cleared, and the following default rule will be restored:
 Send a message when {0}'s brain reaches 1 HP or lower.

Death report settings, discovery records, and in-game entities are unaffected.

LanguageData.CFR.Settings.ResetConfirm:
Reset death report settings?

Two configuration columns will be restored:
 Column 1 sends Major threat letters for the default dangerous entities.
 Column 2 sends messages for all other currently recognized entries.

The current delivery modes, letter styles, entity assignments, and mark monitoring will be replaced with defaults. Contained entity alerts, discovered types, and source expansion are preserved. In-game entities are unaffected.

LanguageData.CFR.Settings.HelpText:
Only replaces notifications for deaths on holding platforms; damage and death rules are unchanged. Each type belongs to at most one configuration column. Unassigned types retain the original vanilla notification conditions and content. Entries owned by another column have a gray background and cannot be edited. Dedicated support covers Anomaly, Held Human and Ratkin Anomaly+; other sources receive generic fallback support.

Initialization and reset create two columns: dangerous defaults in column 1 and all other currently recognized entries in column 2. The columns are independent thereafter. New columns use messages and start empty. Deleting or clearing a column restores vanilla notifications for its entities. Select all transfers all current entries, including collapsed sources and fallback categories, into that column and clears selections elsewhere. Reset removes extra columns and restores default delivery and assignments, but preserves discovery and source expansion.

Entries represent entity races or capturable mutant types, not every shambler's original race. Unknown humanlike races use Held Human's fallback; other unknown types use Other. New types are recorded when rebuilding the settings list scans occupied platforms, or when a contained entity dies. They inherit their fallback category's column, including no assignment. Existing independent entries no longer follow fallback changes.

Death-cause, injury and probability recording rules are unchanged. No per-tick scan is added. Configuration and discovery are stored in global mod settings.

The selected vanilla lethal call records death-on-downed with its actual probability, health death, or a hediff timed-death entry. Health details are read before Kill changes the body, following the vanilla deterministic check order, without re-rolling RNG or re-running potentially side-effecting custom death predicates. Trace state exists only during that call, with no pawn save data or new per-tick sampling.

A single primary cause is shown: destroyed vital parts, death-on-downed, a lethal health condition, required capacity failure, the lethal injury threshold, or a known special mechanism. Paired organs are checked as a functional group; an old single-organ loss is not automatically fatal. Brain destruction does not repeat consciousness loss. Unconfirmed routes say Unknown.

Fatal damage is one DamageInfo supplied to the death call, not injury history or necessarily the HP actually removed. For example, the Ratkin Anomaly+ pocket-watch mechanism supplies 999 but calls death directly; brain removal is an after-effect. An unavailable packet does not mean no earlier injuries. Earlier shocks are never substituted. Vanilla shocks roll 1–3 base damage, split into 2–4 packets that may hit the same part.

Letters show all injured-part totals and missing parts without a count limit. Injury severity keeps decimals; HP uses the game's rounding. Messages skip the full injury list.

LanguageData.CFR.Settings.DeleteColumnConfirm:
Delete configuration {0}?

Its notification settings will be removed. Its entities will become unassigned and use vanilla death notifications; its monitored marks will be disabled. Selections and notification settings in other columns will remain unchanged.

Discovered types and in-game entities are unaffected.
LanguageData.CFR.Settings.ResetExtraColumns: This will also delete the {0} configuration column(s) after the first two. Their notification settings will not be retained. Their currently recognized entities will be reassigned to the first two columns using the default rules.
LanguageData.CFR.Settings.SelectAllConfirm: Assign all currently recognized entries to configuration {0}?\n\nThis includes available marks, entries in collapsed sources and fallback categories. All selections in other columns will be cleared, but their delivery modes and letter styles will remain unchanged.
LanguageData.CFR.Settings.NoColumns: There are no configuration columns. Contained deaths use vanilla notifications. Use Add configuration or Reset to create configurations.
LanguageData.CFR.Settings.ClearDiscoveryConfirm:
Clear records of additionally discovered containment types?

Their individual entries and column assignments will be removed. Other settings and in-game entities are unaffected. Types recognized directly from their definitions are preserved.

If these entities are still on holding platforms, closing and reopening this settings window will discover them again. They will inherit the current assignment of the applicable fallback:
LanguageData.CFR.Settings.ClearDiscoveryOther: Ordinary unknown types use the Other / unrecognized configuration.
LanguageData.CFR.Settings.ClearDiscoveryHeldHuman: Humans and alien races use the corresponding Held Human configuration.
LanguageData.CFR.Settings.ClearDiscoveryUnassigned: If that fallback is unassigned, the rediscovered type will also remain unassigned.
